source.title: Are ResNets Provably Better than Linear Predictors?

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no truncation or document mismatch apparent.
record.tranche_reason: The paper proves theoretical results about residual-network optimization landscapes and gives an SGD guarantee under a modified architecture; it does not run empirical benchmark experiments or test training error on CIFAR.
record.gate_note: Rows record the paper's own theorem-level results on local minima, approximate stationary points, and projected SGD. CIFAR, initialization, and benchmark training-error results are not tested. Cited results from other work are excluded.
record.test_reason: The study proves residual-network landscape and linear-predictor competitiveness results. It does not establish V3's depth-dependent training-error comparison between plain and residual convolutional networks. Neither local-minimum quality nor competitiveness with a linear predictor measures that comparison. Its results also do not test any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the scalar-output landscape guarantee is relative to the best linear predictor and does not itself ensure algorithmic convergence. A separate projected-SGD guarantee applies to a modified architecture with a skip connection directly to the output.
record.recipe_differences: The paper gives theory rather than benchmark experiments. Its main result concerns objective values at local minima; its algorithmic result uses a modified output-level skip connection and projected SGD on a bounded domain.
record.method_sensitivity: The guarantee changes with architecture: the SGD result is for a skip connection directly to the output. The approximate-stationary-point bound depends on boundedness and Lipschitz assumptions.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated smoothness assumptions, scalar-output residual networks have no local minima worse than the best linear predictor; approximate partial stationary points have norm-dependent bounds. A vector-output gradient bound holds when the output matrix has full row rank.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Residual architectures can have optimization-landscape guarantees relative to linear predictors without a guarantee that standard training reaches those objective values.

fits_no_version.finding: For the modified output-level skip architecture, projected SGD has an iterate within O(1/sqrt(T)) of the best permitted linear predictor, under the theorem's boundedness and Lipschitz assumptions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An output-level linear skip connection permits a projected-SGD guarantee of competitiveness with linear predictors.

record.problems: The main local-minimum theorem is geometric and does not establish that gradient-based training reaches such minima. The SGD theorem assumes a modified architecture, bounded convex domain, bounded losses, and Lipschitz conditions. The scalar-output result does not directly establish the corresponding vector-output theorem for all cases; the paper identifies the rank-deficient case as unresolved.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows omitted. Empirical claims cited from prior work are not results of this study.

untested.parts: Training classification error of large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including corrupted labels and effects of size, stopping, and regularization.
Gradient-descent failure frequencies and effects of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth-dependent training degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks and its prevention by identity shortcuts; special-initialization and normalization-free training exceptions.
Effects of initialization on learning speed, signal propagation, and trainable depth.
Recovery, curvature dynamics, and divergence relative to learning-rate stability thresholds.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and corresponding Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: Section 4 additionally shows that large-norm approximate stationary points can remain suboptimal and that regularization or constraints can introduce spurious local minima. These qualify the paper's theoretical guarantees, not any listed claim version.

versions.untested_parts: No empirical CIFAR-10/100 experiments, random-label training, or comparison of network sizes and training duration.
No two-layer ReLU teacher-student experiment or neuron-width sweep.
No comparison of plain and residual convolutional networks by depth or training error on ImageNet/CIFAR; no experiments with special initialization or normalization-free residual networks.
No initialization comparison or study of signal propagation, trainable depth, tanh networks, or 10,000-layer convolutional networks.
No learning-rate sweep, stability-limit measurement, curvature tracking, or divergence experiment.
No batch-normalization speed or learning-rate comparison, nor a Fixup experiment.

rows.subject: residual network x ↦ wᵀ(x + V fθ(x))
rows.size_stated: arbitrarily deep nonlinear residual unit; scalar output
rows.operation_detail: Proves that the optimization objective has no local minimum above the best linear-predictor objective, under stated smoothness and convexity conditions.

conditions.value: twice differentiable and convex in network output
residual unit followed by tunable linear output layer

rows.measure: Objective value at any local minimum compared with the infimum of linear-predictor objective
rows.note: The result is a theorem about local minima, not an empirical guarantee that a training algorithm reaches one.
rows.check: Corollary 1 establishes a scalar-output local-minimum objective bound, not training-error behavior as depth increases. State the corollary's local Lipschitz assumptions explicitly. The final residual transformation V is fully tunable rather than convolutional.

rows.subject: residual network x ↦ wᵀ(x + V fθ(x))
rows.size_stated: arbitrarily deep nonlinear residual unit; scalar output
rows.operation_detail: Bounds the objective at approximate second-order partial stationary points against the best linear predictor within a bounded norm.

conditions.value: bounded convex domain M with stated Lipschitz conditions
linear predictors with norm at most r

rows.measure: Objective suboptimality of approximate stationary points relative to the best bounded linear predictor
rows.note: The bound depends on the approximate-stationarity tolerance and parameter/domain constants; it does not establish an empirical classification-error result.
rows.check: Approximate partial stationarity relative to a bounded linear comparator does not measure V3. Theorem 3's error term is (ε + ε^(1/4)) times polynomial constants; the extracted fourth-root notation should not be read as 4 times sqrt(ε). Its approximation tolerance does not constitute partial observation of V3.

rows.subject: modified residual architecture x ↦ wᵀx + vᵀfθ(x)
rows.operation_detail: Theorem guarantees that projected SGD has an iterate competitive with any fixed linear predictor.

conditions.value: convex product domain M with bounded (w,v), bounded losses, and Lipschitz condition

rows.measure: Objective value of at least one SGD iterate relative to the best linear predictor allowed by the domain
rows.note: This is a theoretical guarantee under a modified architecture and bounded-domain assumptions, not an experiment on benchmark classification error.
rows.check: The projected-SGD guarantee concerns an output-level skip connection and competitiveness with a linear predictor. It provides no comparison across depths or against plain networks, so it does not measure V3.

rows.subject: vector-valued residual network x ↦ W(x + V fθ(x))
rows.operation_detail: Proves a gradient lower bound when the output matrix has full row rank and positive minimum singular value; states that this rules out above-reference stationary points in that case.

conditions.value: W has full row rank and smin(W)>0
differentiable and convex in first argument

rows.measure: Partial-gradient norm lower bound for objective gap above a linear-predictor objective
rows.locator: Appendix A, Theorem 6 and concluding paragraph
rows.note: The result only covers full-row-rank W; the paper says the corresponding argument for the remaining case is unclear.
rows.check: The full-row-rank gradient bound concerns stationary-point objective values, not depth-dependent training error. The unresolved rank-deficient case limits this theorem, but is not evidence limiting V3.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
